error.notSignedIn: Not signed in to a server yet.
error.imageTooLarge: Only images up to 20 MB can be pasted.
error.notConnected: Not connected to the server yet.
error.windowExited: The connection window quit unexpectedly. Please try again.
error.connectionInUse: A connection in use can’t be removed.

open.missing: This path isn’t on this computer; it may be on the server or another computer.
open.program: It would run a program, so it wasn’t opened; it’s shown in its folder instead.
open.tooLarge: The file is over 1 MB and wasn’t copied.
open.notText: This isn’t a text file and wasn’t copied.

upgrade.fromSource: A run from source can’t upgrade itself; build and install a package.
upgrade.unsupported: The client on this system can’t upgrade in the app; download the new version from the release page.
upgrade.othersOpen: Windows of other connections didn’t quit; quit them first, then upgrade.
upgrade.title: Upgrading CC Desk Tunnel
upgrade.macPrepareFailed: Could not prepare the macOS update ({{reason}}). The current app is still available. Please retry.
upgrade.macInstallLocation: This app location cannot be updated automatically. Install the app in an Applications folder you can write to, then retry.
upgrade.macUpdateBusy: Another window is already updating this app. Please try again later.
upgrade.macInvalidBundle: The downloaded app failed version, architecture or signature verification. The update was stopped.
upgrade.macRollback: The update could not finish. Review the reason below before retrying.

tray.stayInBackground: Keep running when the window is closed
tray.backgroundTitle: CC Desk Tunnel is still running
tray.backgroundBody: Click the tray icon to bring the window back; right-click it and choose “Quit” to end the connection.

bridge.badPin: Enter the SHA256 certificate fingerprint from the trusted install details, or leave it empty to verify with a CA.
bridge.pinMismatch: The service certificate fingerprint doesn’t match; the service token wasn’t sent.
bridge.pinMismatchCheck:
The service certificate fingerprint doesn’t match; the service token wasn’t sent.
Check that the “Service certificate fingerprint” is the one given at install; after the server changes its certificate, enter the new fingerprint. If neither changed, this isn’t your server.
bridge.wssOnly: Native mode needs a WSS address without credentials.
bridge.noAnswer:
The server didn’t finish answering within {{seconds}} s.
Check that the network is stable, or try again later; if it keeps happening, check the server log.
bridge.channelPinMismatch:
The execution channel reached a service certificate whose fingerprint doesn’t match; no credentials were sent.
After the control connection was verified, the same address answered with another certificate: make sure the address isn’t hijacked or pointing at several servers.
bridge.silent:
Nothing has come from the server for {{seconds}} s; the connection is gone.
A network, proxy or reverse proxy on the way cut it without telling this computer.
bridge.badServiceMessage:
A message from the server wasn’t recognized.
The client and server may be different versions; upgrade both to the same one.
bridge.tunnelMismatch: The tunnel connection ID doesn’t match.
bridge.readyMismatch: The tunnel ready ID doesn’t match.
bridge.notReady: Not connected to the server yet, or the execution channel isn’t ready.
bridge.channelRefused:
The execution channel wasn’t authorized.
Reconnect; if it keeps happening, make sure the address doesn’t point at another deployment.

connect.via: This connection went through the system proxy {{proxy}}; make sure the proxy works too.
connect.tooLong: The session history exceeds the WebSocket receive limit.
connect.tooMany: Too many failed sign-ins: the server is refusing this computer for now. Try again later.

proxyRefused.what: The system proxy refused to forward the connection to {{target}}.
proxyRefused.whatNamed: The system proxy {{proxy}} refused to forward the connection to {{target}}.
proxyRefused.check: Check the Windows proxy settings, or add the service address to the proxy’s exclusions.

unresolved.what: Can’t resolve the domain {{host}} in the service address.
unresolved.check: Check the address for typos, and that this computer’s network and DNS work.{{via}}

refused.check: The server may not be running, or the port isn’t its control port; behind nginx, make sure nginx is running.{{via}}

timeout.check: Check that the server is online, that its firewall or cloud security group allows this port, and that this computer’s network can reach it.{{via}}

expired.check: Renew it on the server (the deploy script’s certificate command), then reconnect.

notYetValid.what: The service certificate isn’t valid yet.

hostMismatch.what: The service certificate doesn’t match the host name {{host}} in the address.
hostMismatch.check: Connect with the certificate’s domain, or enter the fingerprint given at install under “Service certificate fingerprint”.

untrusted.what: The service certificate isn’t from a trusted authority.
untrusted.check: With a self-signed certificate, enter the SHA256 fingerprint given at install under “Service certificate fingerprint”.

notTls.check: The address should start with wss:// and point at the server’s control port; check the port.{{via}}

gateway.what: The reverse proxy at {{target}} answered {{status}}: the server behind it isn’t running or can’t be reached.
gateway.check: Check on the server that the service is running.

http.what: {{target}} answered HTTP {{status}}; it isn’t this server’s entry point.
http.check: Check the service address; behind nginx, check that WebSocket (the Upgrade header) is forwarded.

reset.check: This usually means the port isn’t this server, or a network device in between cut it; check the address and try again.{{via}}

other.check: Check the service address and the network.{{via}}

otherCode.check: Check the service address and the network.{{via}}

channel.noAnswer:
The execution channel wasn’t ready within {{seconds}} s.
The service token was accepted and this computer’s SSH service started, but the server’s probe command got no answer. {{slow}}, raise the wait time in Settings → Connection.
channel.slow: If the computer or network is slow
channel.slowShell: If the login shell’s startup scripts or the network are slow

component.security: Check “Protection history” in your antivirus or Windows Security: once you’ve checked where the file came from, restore the quarantined file, allow just that file, and reconnect. See “Antivirus and SmartScreen” on the project page.
component.blocked:
{{name}} was blocked by Windows or security software and can’t start (system error {{code}}).
{{hint}}
component.cannotStart:
{{name}} can’t start (system error {{code}}).
Reinstall the app; if it persists, check your security software’s block log.
component.sshdSaid:
The bundled OpenSSH service (sshd.exe) exited{{code}}.
Its output: {{said}}
component.sshdExited:
The bundled OpenSSH service (sshd.exe) exited{{code}}.
Reconnect; if it keeps happening, reinstall the app.
component.notStartedSaid:
This computer’s SSH service didn’t start.
Its output: {{said}}
component.exitedSaid:
This computer’s SSH service exited.
Its output: {{said}}
component.notStarted:
This computer’s SSH service didn’t start.
Usually security software blocked the bundled PowerShell or OpenSSH. {{hint}}
component.exited:
This computer’s SSH service exited.
Reconnect.
component.unsupportedShell:
This computer’s OpenSSH default shell is {{path}}, under which the bundled SSH service can’t run commands.
cmd, PowerShell and Git Bash are supported; in the registry under HKLM\SOFTWARE\OpenSSH, remove DefaultShell and DefaultShellCommandOption or set them back.
component.prepareSlow:
Preparing this computer’s SSH service didn’t finish within {{seconds}} s.
It’s slower when the computer is busy or security software scans each program; reconnect.
component.prepareSaid:
Preparing this computer’s SSH service failed.
{{said}}
component.prepareFailed:
Preparing this computer’s SSH service failed.
Reconnect; if it still fails, reinstall the app.
component.notListening:
This computer’s SSH service didn’t start listening within {{seconds}} s.
It’s slower when the computer is busy or security software scans each program; you can raise the wait time in Settings → Connection.

local.workerTimeout: Starting this computer’s execution service timed out; check the login shell’s startup scripts.
local.workerMissing: Can’t start this computer’s SSH execution service.
local.workerSignalled: This computer’s SSH execution service stopped (signal {{signal}}); reconnect.
local.workerExited: This computer’s SSH execution service stopped (exit code {{code}}); reconnect.
local.workerNotStarted: Can’t set up this computer’s SSH execution service.
local.workerStopped: This computer’s SSH execution service stopped.
local.noSftpServer:
The system’s sftp-server can’t be found.
macOS includes it; on Linux, install OpenSSH’s SFTP server (openssh-sftp-server on Debian / Ubuntu).
local.keygenFailed: Can’t create this connection’s SSH key.

shell.unsupported: Running here needs zsh or bash by absolute path; check the login shell setting.
shell.missing: This computer’s login shell can’t be found; check where zsh or bash is installed.
shell.notExecutable: This computer’s login shell can’t be run; check the permissions of zsh or bash.
shell.timeout: The login shell took too long to start; check its startup scripts for commands that wait or ask for input.
shell.environmentTooLarge: The login shell’s environment variables exceed the size limit.
shell.outputTooLarge: The output of the login shell’s startup scripts exceeds the size limit.
shell.cannotStart: Can’t start this computer’s login shell ({{code}}); check its path and permissions.
shell.cannotStartUnknown: Can’t start this computer’s login shell (unknown error); check its path and permissions.
shell.signalled: The login shell ended abnormally (signal {{signal}}) without a valid environment; check the shell and its startup scripts.
shell.exited: The login shell ended abnormally (exit code {{code}}) without a valid environment; check the shell and its startup scripts.
shell.noEnvironment: The login shell didn’t return a valid environment; check the zsh or bash startup scripts.

download.noInstaller: The server doesn’t provide a client installer.
download.serverFailed:
Downloading the installer from the server failed ({{reason}}).
Try again, or download from the GitHub release page instead.
download.notYet: the server doesn’t have this installer yet
download.badHash: The installer failed verification; the upgrade was abandoned.
download.noManifest:
Can’t read the release details of {{version}} ({{reason}}).
Check that this computer can reach github.com, or get the installer from the server instead.
download.notInManifest: The release details have no installer for this version.
download.otherFile: The installer on the release page isn’t the file the server provides; the upgrade was abandoned.
download.interrupted:
Downloading the installer from GitHub was interrupted ({{reason}}) after {{received}} / {{size}}.
Check the network and try again, or get the installer from the server instead.
download.tooLarge: The installer is larger than the release details say; the upgrade was abandoned.
download.macNoManifest: Couldn’t read the release details for {{version}} ({{reason}}). Check your connection to GitHub, or download the macOS installer from the release page.
download.macInterrupted: Downloading the macOS installer from GitHub was interrupted ({{reason}}) after {{received}} / {{size}}. Check your connection and try again, or download it from the release page.

service.tooOld: Server {{service}} is too old: run the install command on the server again to upgrade it (see “Quick start” in the project README).
service.manual: Server {{version}} needs a new image: run sudo cc-desk-tunnel upgrade on the server; older deployments without that command run the install command again.
service.noNewer: The server found no newer release.
service.closed: The connection to the server was lost; reconnect in a moment to see whether it has upgraded.

files.missing: The file or folder doesn’t exist.
files.protected: Permission denied. The server’s keys, sign-in credentials and data are protected and can’t be read or changed.
files.denied: No permission to access this location.
files.exists: A file or folder with that name is already there.
files.noServer: The server doesn’t provide file access.
files.unreachable: This computer can’t be reached now: it may be offline, or its execution channel isn’t ready.

ccdt.noTerminal: No terminal app to open was found: run ccdt open in a terminal.
ccdt.badAddress: This connection’s address can’t be handed to ccdt.

connections.nameTooLong: Names can be at most {{max}} characters.
connections.nameTaken: A connection with that name already exists.
connections.tooMany: At most {{max}} connections can be saved.
connections.stillOpen: This connection’s window is still open; quit it first.

macos.desktop: Access the projects you choose in your Desktop folder, so Claude can read and change their files through the execution channel.
macos.documents: Access the projects you choose in your Documents folder, so Claude can read and change their files through the execution channel.
macos.downloads: Access the projects you choose in your Downloads folder, so Claude can read and change their files through the execution channel.
macos.removable: Access the projects you choose on removable volumes, so Claude can read and change their files through the execution channel.
macos.network: Access the projects you choose on network volumes, so Claude can read and change their files through the execution channel.
